17 	[Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/glossary#partial-prefetching) changes what a `<Link>` downloads for a Cache Components route. With Partial Prefetching enabled, a `<Link>` prefetches the route's [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell): its static content and the cached content that doesn't depend on the URL. Build and typecheck both pass. Here's what I changed and why.

## What changed

app/product/page.tsx — related products are now deferred out of the default prefetch:
- Extracted the related-products list into an async <RelatedProducts> component wrapped in <Suspense> (fallback: "Loading related products...").
- await prefetchStage() sits above the getRelatedProducts() call. Per the prefetch() API docs, this keeps the subtree out of the route's App Shell (the default prefetch every <Link> into the route downloads) while still allowing it to be resolved by a per-link prefetch or on navigation. getRelatedProducts() stays 'use cache' with cacheLife('hours'), so the per-link prefetch can resolve it from cache.
- export const prefetch = 'partial' opts this one route into Partial Prefetching incrementally, without flipping the global partialPrefetching flag (the docs' recommended path for adopting one route at a time). cacheComponents was already enabled in next.config.ts.
- Imported the prefetch() function as prefetchStage to avoid the naming collision with the prefetch route-segment export (called out in both the prefetch() function and route-segment-config docs).

app/page.tsx — the featured-product link now opts into the per-link prefetch:
- <Link href="/product" prefetch={true}> triggers a per-link prefetch that resolves the product page's URL/cached content — including the deferred related products — before the click, so they render immediately on navigation.

## How the two halves meet

| Stage | What's ready |
|---|---|
| Default <Link> into /product (App Shell) | Heading, description, and the "Loading related products..." fallback — not the list |
| Featured-product <Link prefetch={true}> (per-link prefetch) | Above plus the resolved related-products list, before the click |
| Navigation | Everything, instantly when arriving via the featured link |

I chose prefetch() rather than navigation() deliberately: navigation() would also exclude the list from per-link prefetches (rendering only on navigation), which would contradict "have them ready immediately when navigating from the featured-product link." prefetch() is the primitive that excludes from the shell but includes in the per-link prefetch.

## Verification
- npm run build → exit 0. Product route prerendered static with Revalidate 1h (from cacheLife('hours')); Cache Components enabled.
- npx tsc --noEmit → exit 0.

One caveat worth flagging: prefetching only runs in production builds (per the Link docs), so this behavior isn't observable in next dev — the dev server renders everything on request. To assert the prefetched-vs-deferred split at runtime, the docs describe an instant() Playwright test (@next/playwright) against a production build; I didn't add one since none existed and the task was about the wiring, but I can add that regression test if you'd like.
